# Full-space tilted-mean balance without cap regularity

This extends the attained full-affine negative-power buffer framework. At an UNPENALIZED joint local minimum below the atomic parity bound, the tilted FULL mixed centroid belongs to the convex hull of the actual proper-gap deepest marks. No regular cap circuit, section derivative, or singleton-contact premise is required. The proof uses strict finite changes and the already proved all-atomic hinge erosion. It does not identify the tilted law with the original uniform mixed law or prove a Gamma payment.

## 1. Setting and precise conclusion

Let P be a finite complete canonical lattice base, and K_z positive compatible d-dimensional convex fibers, d>=1. Set C=conv union_z({z} times K_z), mu=sum_z vol_d on these fibers, M=mu(C), and k=k(P). Work in aff(P) times R^d. Fix epsilon>0, N=d+1, r>=d, and a strictly positive affine full-space function L on compact C with

    <L^(-r)>=M^(-1) integral L^(-r)dmu=1.

Use

    f(w)=[L(w) E_(C_z)(X)/M]^(1/N),  w=(z,X),

and the actual within-fiber covariance norm G on continuous normals. At w=(p,y), the raw buffered depth b_L(w) is the infimum of the masses of

    a.(z-p)+u.(X-y)>=-epsilon f(w) G(u),

over u nonzero and arbitrary base a, also minimized with the closed weighted pure-base depth b_base(p). Write

    Q=max_(w in S) b_L(w),
    I={p in P: max_(y in K_p) b_L(p,y)=Q},
    J={p in I: b_base(p)>Q},
    A=I\J,
    W_J={(p,y):p in J, b_L(p,y)=Q}.

Assume that (K,L) is a joint local minimum of Q/M over actual positive compatible families and their normalized positive full-affine parameters, and that

    0<Q/M<1/k.                                             (1)

Then J is nonempty and

    g_L := integral_S w L(w)^(-r-1)dmu
                         / integral_S L(w)^(-r-1)dmu
             belongs to conv(W_J).                         (2)

The stronger numerical bad premise Q/M<Gamma_d/k implies (1), but Gamma_d does not enter this proof. The local minimum must be unpenalized; no penalty derivative is discarded.

Dependencies used below are the fixed-positive-body buffered continuity and finite tilt-compression results, the actual whole-own-fiber/base-gap lemma, ordinary joint energy-root concavity with marked-homothety equality, and `candidate f324bc23ceb65e89`. The extension of the last theorem to the present normalization is proved in Section 4.

## 2. Proper maximizing marks and strict local parameter decrease

All deepest marks are fiber-interior. At a fiber-boundary mark E=f=0. A supporting continuous normal extends to a full affine supporting plane of the canonical finite family by the finite support LP. The captured support traces have zero d-volume in every fiber, so the buffered depth there is zero. This also holds for d=1. Thus W_J is a compact subset of the union of the relative fiber interiors: the deepest sets are closed in the compact sampled fibers, and their boundaries are disjoint from them.

At any w in W_J, an active nonvertical cap of mass Q is attained. Indeed Q<b_base(p) excludes a pure-base infimum; the finite status-pattern tilt-compression result gives bounded base-tilt representatives, after normalizing G(u)=1, and cap-mass continuity gives attainment. Its own trace is proper: a full own trace would give mass at least b_base(p) by the actual whole-fiber capture lemma. The trace cannot be empty because y is interior and the positive buffer captures a neighborhood on its side of the through-y plane. The other fibers may have arbitrary supporting incidences.

Here is the precise strict comparison needed later. At such an old deepest mark w, if a new positive parameter L' satisfies L'(w)<L(w), then

    b_(L')(w)<Q.                                         (3)

Keep one attained old normal and base tilt fixed. Its new threshold moves strictly upward, since E(w)>0 and f depends strictly increasingly on L(w). The own threshold moves from one value strictly below u.y to another strictly below u.y. The old own threshold is inside the projected support interval. The intervening strip therefore has positive d-volume. Every other fiber can only lose captured mass. This fixed actual cap has new mass strictly below Q, proving (3). No coarea differentiability is used.

More generally, at every point where L'<=L one has b_(L')<=b_L. If the old value is less than Q this already gives a strict upper bound by Q; if the old value is Q at a proper-gap base, (3) gives the strict bound.

## 3. A uniform neighborhood argument and exact parameter step

Suppose g_L does not belong to conv(W_J), temporarily assuming J nonempty. Compactness permits strict affine separation: there is one affine full-space psi such that

    psi(g_L)=0,       psi(w)<=-eta<0 for every w in W_J.  (4)

The first equality gives <L^(-r-1)psi>=0. For small positive t define the EXACT normalized parameter

    L_t=[<(L+t psi)^(-r)>]^(1/r)(L+t psi).               (5)

Strict positivity of L on compact C makes this legal for both signs near zero. Differentiating the scalar normalization, or using its uniform Taylor expansion, gives

    L_t=L+t psi+o(t) uniformly on C.                     (6)

Choose a relatively open neighborhood U of W_J in the union of the fibers at bases J, with psi<=-eta/2 on its closure. For all sufficiently small positive t,

    L_t<L on U.                                         (7)

The complement of U in those finitely many compact fibers has no old maximizing mark. By upper semicontinuity of the old depth its maximum is at most Q-kappa for some kappa>0, unless that complement is empty. Fixed-body uniform parameter continuity then keeps every new value there below Q. On U, pointwise monotonicity and (3) show every new value is strictly below Q: either its old value was already below Q, or it was an old proper-gap deepest mark. The new depth maximum is attained on each compact fiber, so

    max_(y in K_p) b_(L_t)(p,y)<Q for EVERY p in J.       (8)

This step does not infer a uniform positive loss from pointwise strict inequalities. Instead it combines a uniform old gap outside U with an exact comparison inside U and attainment of the new maximum. No quantitative coarea lower bound is needed.

The required fixed-body uniform continuity also has a direct all-normal proof. If all K_z lie in R Ball, every section perpendicular to a unit u has area at most omega_(d-1) R^(d-1), with omega_0=1. Changing f to f_t moves any cap threshold by epsilon G(u)|f_t-f|, regardless of its integer tilt. Its total mass therefore changes by at most

    |P| omega_(d-1) R^(d-1) epsilon G_max ||f_t-f||_infinity,

where G_max=max_(||u||=1)G(u). Taking the infimum over all caps preserves this bound, and pure-base cap masses are unchanged. Positive uniform L_t convergence gives uniform f_t convergence. The same slab estimate with the additional source displacement proves continuity on each fixed fiber, hence attainment of its maximum. This proof includes supporting facets and all oblique base tilts.

At each old atomic base p in A, the unchanged pure-base depth bounds the entire new fiber by Q, regardless of how L_t varies there. At every base outside I the finite old gap persists by the same uniform continuity. Therefore the new global raw maximum Q_t satisfies

    Q_t<=Q.

If Q_t<Q, the parameter change is already a strict local descent. If Q_t=Q, every new maximizing base lies in A and has b_base(p)=Q. Thus the new positive pair is entirely atomic at its actual maximizing bases. Section 4 supplies a subsequent arbitrarily small strict body descent. Both steps can be chosen within any prescribed neighborhood of the old pair, contradicting local minimality. This proves (2) once J is known nonempty. If J were empty initially, Section 4 directly gives the contradiction, proving nonemptiness as well.

## 4. All-atomic hinge cleanup with full-space normalization

The geometric and numerical hinge proof requires only joint concavity of f, positivity and continuity of the parameter, and unchanged pure-base cap costs. These hold here.

For completeness, suppose every current maximizing base is atomic, with raw maximum Q and deepest-base parity count k(I), and Q/M<1/k(I). Convexity of the real buffered Q-superlevel makes I midpoint-closed. The maximal-threshold argument compresses finitely many mass-Q pure-base caps into m<=k(I) mass-Q caps G_i covering I. Choose nonnegative convex base hinges h_i with sampled support exactly P intersect G_i, and normalize their surface costs D_i=sum_z S_z h_i(z). The actual compatible inner erosions

    K_z(s)=K_z eroded by s h(z) Ball,
    h=sum_i h_i/D_i,

have total first mass loss m and captured first loss at least 1 in every G_i. The fixed pure-base caps therefore give

    M_(G_i)(s)/M(s)
        <=Q/M-s[1-(Q/M)m]/M+o(s)<Q/M.                  (9)

All inclusions are preserved because h is convex in the base; the source proof treats every incoming anchored relation and arbitrary nonsmooth fibers.

Retain the old affine L and renormalize it on the NEW actual family by

    L_s=c_s L,
    c_s=[M(s)^(-1) integral_(S(s)) L^(-r)dmu]^(1/r).    (10)

The eroded canonical body is contained in the old one, so L remains strictly positive. Its inverse-power kernel is bounded and continuous there. Positive Hausdorff convergence and volume convergence give c_s->1. Thus L_s is a legal positive full-space affine parameter and varies continuously; the new covariance and energies do too. Bases outside the old I retain their strict gap. Pure-base caps in (9) cover every mark over I independently of these parameter changes. Consequently the actual global normalized maximum decreases strictly.

No source gradient or projective-centroid alignment appears in this cleanup. Under (1), Q/M<1/k(P)<=1/k(I), so it applies at either stage of Section 3.

## 5. Actual marked-fiber rigidity and status heredity

These are fixed-family facts; neither parameter optimality nor (1) is needed. Suppose r in J has an anchored representation r=sum_j lambda_j p_j by deepest bases p_j in I with all lambda_j>0. Choose ANY corresponding deepest marks w_j=(p_j,y_j). Their affine combination w_r lies in the convex buffered Q-superlevel, in the actual r-fiber, and is therefore deepest. Choose a proper-own attained active cap there, normalize G(u)=1, and write

    H={Nw>=c},    c=Nw_r-epsilon f_r,    mu(H)=Q.

The upper tail for N is continuous and strictly decreasing near c because of its proper own trace at r. Hence its right Q-quantile is exactly c. Every input deepest mark satisfies

    Nw_j-epsilon f_j<=c.

Averaging and comparing with concavity of f forces

    f_r=sum_j lambda_j f_j,
    Nw_j-epsilon f_j=c for every j.                    (11)

Put L_j=L(w_j), L_r=L(w_r). Unlike a merely concave base parameter, full-space affinity gives L_r=sum_j lambda_j L_j EXACTLY. Equality in the geometric-mean concavity chain for f=F^(d/N)L^(1/N)/M^(1/N) now forces energy-root equality and constant F_j/L_j. The full marked-homothety equality theorem, including strict energy monotonicity under a proper target inclusion, yields one convex body D with

    K_(p_j)=y_j+L_j D,
    K_r=y_r+L_r D,
    f_j/L_j=f_r/L_r=c_*>0.                             (12)

The common actual cap H has in EVERY such marked fiber the normalized own trace

    {Y in D:u.Y>=-epsilon c_*}.                        (13)

It is proper at r, so it is proper at every input. But at an atomic deepest mark every own buffered trace is full: otherwise adding a sufficiently large finite base tilt from a mass-Q atomic cap produces mass strictly below Q. Thus no p_j can be atomic. This proves proper-gap heredity for the full-space parameter.

The same argument gives at most one proper deepest mark per base. If two distinct such marks shared a base, their midpoint would have a proper attained cap, and (11) would force equality in f's fixed-fiber concavity. But F=E^(1/d) is strictly concave on the interior of a fixed positive body by marked-homothety equality; multiplication in the positive weighted geometric mean with affine L preserves that strictness. This is impossible. Hence W_J is in fact finite, although the proof in Sections 2–3 only needed compactness.

As in the audited base-only status theorem, J is a closed minor, A is a closed minor, and the atomic mass-Q cover can be selected with at most k(I)-k(J) caps: selected atomic witnesses have distinct parities, and none shares parity with a point of J. A midpoint of two witnesses would be deepest; heredity makes it atomic, contradicting the threshold cover. A midpoint of one witness and a J point is either proper, contradicting heredity, or atomic, contradicting the same strict threshold inequalities. These claims retain the actual selected cap boundaries and do not assert that ALL parities of A are disjoint from those of J.

## 6. What the full-space conclusion adds and does not add

The density L^(-r-1) is strictly positive on every actual fiber. The same supporting-affine-function argument as for the uniform mixed centroid shows g_L lies in relint(C). Equation (2) therefore places a point of relint(C) in the convex hull of the actual proper deepest MARKS, not merely in the convex hull of their integer bases. In particular the proper stratum cannot be contained in an exposed face of C.

This does not imply conv(W_J)=C, that all deepest marks are proper, or that the original uniform mixed mean belongs to conv(W_J). The equality/status argument is restricted to genuine anchored representations with proper deepest targets. Finally the source gradient remains

    grad_X log f_L=a_E+grad_X L/(N L),

so none of these statements restores the old energy-centroid alignment or its Gamma boundary payment. The new balance is a rigorous full-space necessary condition, with the changed alignment still retained.

## 7. Sharp limitation: every interior point is a realizable tilted mean

The following observation is due to the contributor. For the SAME fixed positive compatible family and every prescribed y in relint(C), there is exactly one normalized positive full-affine L whose tilted mean g_L equals y. The point y need not lie in an actual sampled fiber; when it does, no depth property of that mark is required.

Translate y to the relative origin and minimize

    I_y(a)=M^(-1) integral_S [1+a.(w-y)]^(-r)dmu       (14)

over charts strictly positive on C. Because C contains a relative ball about y, this coefficient domain is bounded. Its closure is compact. Every boundary chart has a zero on C and hence at some sampled fiber point. The inverse-power divergence theorem for r>=d, including its joint-limit form, gives I_y(a_j)->infinity as a_j approaches that boundary. Since a=0 is admissible, a minimum is therefore attained in the positive domain.

The function is strictly convex there. Indeed t->t^(-r) is strictly convex, and distinct coefficient vectors cannot agree almost everywhere on S: an affine function zero on each full-dimensional sampled fiber has zero continuous coefficient and zero base restriction on P, hence is zero on the full relative span. Differentiation at the unique minimum a_y is legal by uniform chart positivity and yields

    integral_S (w-y)[1+a_y.(w-y)]^(-r-1)dmu=0.        (15)

Set L=I_y(a_y)^(1/r)[1+a_y.(w-y)]. It has <L^(-r)>=1 and g_L=y. Conversely, if a normalized positive affine L has g_L=y, write it as L(y)[1+a.(w-y)]. Equation (15) makes a stationary for the strictly convex I_y, hence a=a_y; normalization fixes L(y)=I_y(a_y)^(1/r). This proves uniqueness as well as existence.

For an explicit ordinary calibration, let S=C=[0,1], r=2, and 0<y<1. Then

    L_y(x)=[y+(1-2y)x]/sqrt[y(1-y)]

is positive on the interval, has integral_0^1 L_y^(-2)dx=1, and its L_y^(-3)-weighted mean is exactly y. Thus even arbitrarily shallow interior marks can be made their own tilted means.

This does not contradict (2): that theorem couples the tilted mean to a JOINT minimizing buffer and its actual proper deepest set. It proves that the full-space moment inclusion, when detached from that variational premise, imposes no depth restriction. No mean-lift or Gamma payment follows from (2) alone.
